chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, then she is entitled to half of her dowry. And if he had not specified a dowry for her,
then provision should be made in a fair manner, according to the means of the wealthy and according to the means of the poor.
And there is no waiting period for her; she may marry whomever she wishes immediately.

key_terms.بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ: in a fair and customary manner
key_terms.طَلَّقَ: divorced; the act of issuing divorce
key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: waiting period a woman observes before remarrying
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: provision or compensatory gift given fairly
key_terms.مَهْرِهَا: her dowry, the marriage dower due to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry and ʿiddah if a woman is divorced before consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for a woman divorced before consummation. It states that she receives half the dowry if one was specified, or a fair compensatory provision based on the husband's means if none was specified. It also clarifies that she has no ʿiddah in this case and may remarry immediately.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4773 - Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as) that he said:

"If a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, she is entitled to half of her dowry. However, if he had not specified a dowry for her, then 'provision must be made for her in a fair manner', 'according to the means of the wealthy and according to the means of the poor.'
She does not have to observe any waiting period (iddah) and may marry whomever she wishes immediately."
